item.title: OpenAI Ends Cursor Access After SpaceX Acquisition
item.description: Cursor's founder confirms OpenAI will end direct model access after the acquisition.
item.content:encoded:
Cursor's founder confirms OpenAI will end direct model access after the acquisition.

Original source: https://openai.com/index/our-decision-on-cursor-following-its-acquisition-by-spacex/

Digg story: https://digg.com/tech/cpbd83av

OpenAI announced it will terminate Cursor's direct access to its models following the coding tool's acquisition by SpaceX. The change takes effect in three months. Cursor co-founder and CEO Michael Truell stated that OpenAI models currently handle about 5 percent of user traffic and said the company is speaking with OpenAI to resolve the issue. Cursor was an early user of OpenAI models. Observers including Miles Brundage and Matthew Berman linked the decision to concerns over SpaceX and Elon Musk. Amjad Masad of Replit offered free OpenAI model access on its platform as an alternative.

item.title: OpenAI Researcher Explains Selective Math Result Announcements
item.description: Noam Brown says OpenAI announces internal model math results only when they shift views on AI progress.
item.content:encoded:
Noam Brown says OpenAI announces internal model math results only when they shift views on AI progress.

Original source: https://openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics/

Digg story: https://digg.com/tech/gilz6cyc

Noam Brown, an OpenAI research engineer, posted on X that the company devotes resources to announcing math results from internal models like Astra only when the findings would meaningfully change people’s understanding of AI progress. He added that the main focus remains shipping great models so the public can use them. The post follows an earlier announcement that an internal Astra version solved ten open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science. It drew replies on X and was retweeted by fellow researcher Mo Bavarian.

item.title: Chamath Palihapitiya Says AI Long-Horizon Tasks Still Fail
item.description: Quote from a Stanford AI Club talk draws agreement from Gary Marcus on AI limits.
item.content:encoded:
Quote from a Stanford AI Club talk draws agreement from Gary Marcus on AI limits.

Original source: https://garymarcus.substack.com/p/misplaced-panic-over-ai-progress

Digg story: https://digg.com/tech/52lmg3vp

Rohan Paul posted a quote from Chamath Palihapitiya speaking at the Stanford AI Club. Chamath stated that long-horizon tasks remain a joke and current AI does not handle them. He added that complex problems also do not work and warned of a hype cycle that will lead to contraction and a trough of disillusionment. Gary Marcus replied that Chamath was right and linked to an earlier post of his own making the same point.

Steven Dillmann announced the release of Terminal-Bench-Science, a benchmark for AI agents on research workflows. Version 0.1 contains 70 tasks spanning life, physical, earth, mathematical, and engineering sciences. Each task was contributed by a researcher adapting their own workflows into agentic challenges on problems they care about. The project is an ongoing Stanford-led community effort built by the Terminal-Bench team together with domain experts at research institutions worldwide. Dillmann stated that it discriminates between frontier models similarly to Terminal-Bench 3.0 while lowering pass rates for every model tested on both.
